mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate strengthening residential construction and consumer confidence, which typically precedes higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. This relationship holds consistently across economic cycles without requiring specific threshold conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods where HOUST increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.05 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.1% signals aggressive monetary easing, which reduces discount rates for equity valuations and stimulates economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.1%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in payrolls (PAYEMS) and decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a robust labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint effect of PAYEMS rising and UNRATE falling does not produce positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances, or the interaction term in a regression model has a negative coefficient with p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: During a post-pandemic supply shock recovery, rising industrial production (INDPRO) signals improving manufacturing output and economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO rises by at least 0.5% month-over-month during the supply shock recovery regime, or the Rank IC is below 0.04 over any 1-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Rising consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicates increasing inflationary pressures, which typically lead to tighter monetary policy and reduced equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when CPIAUCSL rises by at least 0.2% month-over-month, or the Rank IC is above -0.05 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1200 thousand units, it signals a strong housing market and elevated consumer confidence, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when HOUST > 1200, or the Rank IC is below 0.04 over any 6-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a high unemployment regime (UNRATE > 10%), a high unemployment rate (UNRATE) is associated with weak consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE > 10%, or the Rank IC is above -0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in CPI (CPIAUCSL) and decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates a monetary policy response to inflation, which typically stabilizes the economy and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint effect of CPIAUCSL rising and FEDFUNDS falling does not produce positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances, or the interaction term in a regression model has a negative coefficient with p-value > 0.05.
